chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Where is the place of the two Rak'at that are before the morning prayer?' He said: 'Before the emergence of the dawn. So when the dawn emerges, the time for the morning prayer has entered.'
ai.seo_question: When should the two Sunnah Rak'at of the morning prayer be performed relative to the dawn?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the precise boundary between the Sunnah and Fard of the morning prayer, a distinction crucial in Shia jurisprudence for ensuring the validity of voluntary acts before the obligatory time commences. By defining the moment of Fajr's emergence as the cutoff, the Imam clarifies that the two Rak'at are distinct from the four Sunnahs often prayed after Fajr, emphasizing the importance of timely adherence to the prescribed prayer windows.
